note: Read 2026-11-01 at the owner's word ("Build those first 3 starting with ledger first"; of the 21 countries read first: "It should cover across every country"; "Retry the blocked tax facts once all countries land"): the tax on a screen worker's pay in Kuwait: a resident's income tax, social contributions, what is withheld at source, a non-resident artiste's withholding, an author's treatment, VAT and the tax year. Research and retry subagents (workbench/briefs/BRIEF-tax.md, BRIEF-tax-retry.md), every quote checked by the lead against its saved page.

figures.finding: Kuwait levies no personal income tax: the Income Tax Decree, as amended in 2008, imposes income tax only on bodies corporate carrying on business in Kuwait, so an individual's pay and fees are not taxed.

sources.said: An annual Income Tax is hereby imposed on the income of every body corporate, wherever incorporated, carrying on trade or business by the activity in the State of Kuwait
The term (taxpayer) means any body corporate subject to the income tax imposed by this Decree.
There is no personal income tax (PIT) imposed on individuals in Kuwait.

figures.finding: With no personal income tax there is no individual tax year or return; the taxable period in the Decree is a body corporate's.

sources.said: The term (taxpayer) means any body corporate subject to the income tax imposed by this Decree.

figures.finding: Social security covers Kuwaiti employees only: the employer pays 11.5% and the employee 8% of monthly salary up to KWD 2,750, plus 2.5% from the employee up to KWD 1,500 from 2015; expatriate workers pay none and are owed an end-of-service indemnity instead.

value.indemnity: 15 days' pay per year for the first three years, 2/3 month's pay per year thereafter (after three years' service)

figures.applies: Kuwaiti employees under the Social Security Law; no performers' scheme found

sources.said: For Kuwaiti employees, contributions are payable monthly by both the employer and employee under the Social Security Law. The employer’s contribution is 11.5% and the employee’s is 8% of monthly salary, up to a ceiling of 2,750 Kuwaiti dinars (KWD) per month.

effective 1 January 2015, the employee’s contribution under the Social Security Law will increase by 2.5% of the monthly salary, up to a ceiling of KWD 1,500 per month. Currently, there are no social security obligations for expatriate workers in Kuwait.

figures.finding: Nothing is withheld from an individual's pay or fee: Kuwaiti law has no withholding tax; the 5% retention pending a tax clearance applies only to payments to incorporated bodies.

sources.said: Kuwaiti tax law does not impose withholding tax (WHT). However, all public bodies and private entities are required to retain 5% from the contract, agreement, or transaction value or from each payment made to any incorporated body

figures.finding: A non-resident performer, writer or director working in Kuwait as an individual pays no Kuwaiti income tax and has nothing withheld; only a body corporate (a loan-out company, for one) carrying on business in Kuwait is taxed.

value.note: a body corporate is taxed at 15% under the Decree (not read here)

sources.said: An annual Income Tax is hereby imposed on the income of every body corporate, wherever incorporated, carrying on trade or business by the activity in the State of Kuwait
The domestic tax law in Kuwait does not provide for WHTs.

figures.finding: With no personal income tax and no withholding, an author's fees and royalties paid to an individual are untaxed; no special regime exists or is needed.

sources.said: There is no personal income tax (PIT) imposed on individuals in Kuwait.

figures.finding: Kuwait has no VAT: it signed the GCC VAT framework in 2017 but has not enacted it.

sources.said: In Kuwait, the GCC framework agreement is currently under discussion in the Parliament while the draft Law is under preparation by the government.
